text: Every video must have a proper thumbnail/cover, and its text must hedge exactly like the narration (same qualifiers, no stronger claim than the voiceover makes).
evidence: black-october: Owner: 'Every video needs a proper thumbnail... The cover must hedge exactly like the narration.' | retired: the cover is made by frameflow.cover, whose prompt already requires the narration's hedges

text: Keep a single ending beat after the payoff (one closing question or one practical takeaway, not both stacked) and a short tail (about 10 s or less); fold any extra stat into the scene before. Never write a follow call to action: the pipeline's end card adds it.
evidence: black-october: Owner: 'an outro call to action (follow)'. Review: three endings run back to back in the 18s tail after the payoff.; again in black-october

text: Never leave a frame near-empty while the narrator is speaking: every key phrase (stat, rating, quote intro) needs its visual on screen from the first frame and held until the line ends. Check keyframes at each narration cue for blank pages.
evidence: black-october: Scene 5 at 29s faint kicker only during 'rated nine point', Scene 8 blank page at 43s during 'Chainguard's CEO says', cake missing before Scene 6, and Scene 10 sky text appearing early over the wrong line.; again in black-october

text: When revising a script, keep the first draft's voice, jokes and rhythm; fix only what the notes name. In a blind test the owner preferred the first draft over the final revised one.
evidence: black-october: blind A/B on 2026-10-25, Talha chose script-v1 over script (final).

text: Make the script flow for a first-time viewer: every part should lead into the next, and when the story moves on, the viewer should know what is being answered now and why. Use whatever fits the moment (a spoken question, a 'but' or 'so', a callback, a quick bridge) and vary it; never just jump to an answer the viewer wasn't set up for.
evidence: black-october: Owner: some questions are asked aloud ('The cause?') while others appear only as an on-screen heading and the narrator jumps into the answer. It should be consistent so the audience can follow.

text: Time each reveal visual to its narration cue and in the storyboard order. Show the big number, the object or the quote card on the cue word, hold it until the line ends, and don't show later text early.
evidence: black-october: 'RATED 9.2' caption didn't render at 'rated nine point'. The 14-candle cake never showed. The sky said 'NOT EVEN YOU' from 57s, before 'Not you'.

text: After the payoff, run one ending beat only. Fold any extra stat into the preceding action scene rather than adding another closing scene, and keep the tail after the payoff short (about 10s or less).
evidence: black-october: Pacing: three endings ran back to back (Censys stat, to-do note, finders-or-fixers question) in an 18s tail after the payoff. | merged into L2

text: Keep the picture in step with the voice: headings, labels and on-screen questions should match what is being said at that moment and help the viewer follow where the story is going, not introduce a question or point the narration never makes.
evidence: black-october (Talha's feedback): 'HOW COMMON IS PHP?' and 'HOW BAD? HOW OLD?' were shown as headings while the narrator jumped straight to the answers; other questions were asked aloud. Pairs with L5.
